objective: Reduce a benchmark-facing automatic-fail risk by replacing two legacy rigid Cube futon renderers with physically reasoned, render-only household bedding drapes that wrap the actual balcony top rail, retain slab clearance, use rough dielectric textile response and preserve LOD0/1/2/3 silhouette stability. No rendered-quality credit is awarded without native Unity pixels.

fix: close futon drape installation envelope
quality: add futon construction and material contract

quality: gate futon drapes in native 4K packet

sourceFinding.criticalRisk: Futon_2_1 and Futon_3_4 originate as benchmark-facing built-in Cube renderers and were not covered by the structural-surface replacement path inspected in this run. The legacy rigid slab therefore remained eligible to trigger the visible primitive-placeholder critical fail.
sourceFinding.constructionConflict: Legacy source dimensions place an approximately 0.82 m tall rigid futon slab such that its lower edge reaches roughly 0.10 m into the balcony-slab envelope, which is incompatible with a textile being aired over the rail and risks visible hero interpenetration.
sourceFinding.priorityReason: A visible primitive or hero interpenetration is an automatic Visual Fidelity FAIL, so removing this risk has higher expected score utility than adding new decorative microdetail.

manufactureInstallationDecision.mounting: Gravity-balanced drape around the actual RailTop renderer bounds; no invisible rigid bracket was invented.
manufactureInstallationDecision.geometryVsMaterial: Centimetre-scale loft, rail wrap, front/back drop, sag and hems are geometry. Thread weave, fine fibre breakup, restrained wash/UV variation and angular textile response are material/microdetail. Illumination is never baked into albedo.
manufactureInstallationDecision.exposureAging: Dry midsummer exterior state with ordinary UV/wash/fold variation. No current wet sheen, arbitrary tears or unexplained dirt mask.

materialDefinition.microstructure: Generated 512 px deterministic asymmetric warp/weft plus fibre breakup; mipmapped, trilinear, anisotropy 8, physically tiled at 0.14 m.
materialDefinition.fresnel: rough dielectric only; no metallic edge flash, emission or painted highlight

lodDefinition.invariants: All levels retain the U-shaped rail wrap, closed thickness and occupancy silhouette; vertex count must decrease monotonically and macro renderer bounds stay within 18 mm size / 10 mm center of LOD0.

selfAudit.finding: The first parameter pass left the second drape approximately 115 mm above the balcony floor, outside the declared 30-90 mm construction envelope.
selfAudit.correction: Adjusted the second front/back drops to 0.680/0.515 m. Source geometry math now predicts approximately 81 mm lower-edge clearance; the first drape predicts approximately 57 mm.
selfAudit.policy: Corrected geometry rather than relaxing the QA threshold.

selfAudit.finding: Static triangle cross-product audit found the first closed side-hem implementation wound its lateral faces inward, risking backface-culling holes at oblique/grazing angles.
selfAudit.correction: Reversed the lateral hem winding to outward -X/+X and added fail-closed ValidateOutwardHemWinding checks to every generated LOD mesh.
selfAudit.policy: No render-quality claim is made from the source audit alone.
